editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.
scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for ŚB 11.10.1–11.10.37; the pinned source group 11.10.27–11.10.29.

entries.sanskrit:
चतुर्-विंशति-गुर्व्-आख्या लब्ध-संभावनाभुवः ।

उद्धवस्यात्म-तत्त्वाप्त्यै साधनोक्तिर् अतः परैः ॥

दशमे देह-संबन्धात् संसृतिर् नात्मनः स्वतः ।

इत्य् एतद् वर्णयाम् आस मतान्तर-निरासतः ॥

तद् एवम् अन्वय-व्यतिरेकाभ्याम् उत्पन्न-विवेक-ज्ञानस्य तत्त्व-ज्ञानायादित आरभ्य साधनान्य् उपदिशति भगवान्---मयेति । मया पञ्चरात्राद्य्-उक्त-वैष्णव-धर्मेष्व् अवहितोऽप्रमत्तः संस् तद् अविरोधेन वर्णाद्य्-आचारम् अनुतिष्ठेत् ॥१॥
word_for_word: the account of the twenty-four gurus
for Uddhava's attainment of the truth of the Self
because of connection with the body
not of the Self by itself
in Vaiṣṇava duties taught by the Pāñcarātra and other texts
entries.literal_english: The twenty-four-guru account has prepared Uddhava for knowledge of the Self. Here the Lord begins to teach the means of truth through positive and negative analysis. Transmigration belongs to connection with the body, not to the Self by itself. One should therefore attentively follow the Vaiṣṇava duties taught by the Pāñcarātra and similar texts, together with conduct appropriate to one's social class and stage, without contradiction between them.

entries.sanskrit: कथम् अकामात्मता संभवति ? तत्राह---अन्वीक्षेतेति । स्व-धर्मैर् विशुद्ध-चित्तः सन् देहिनां विषयेषु सत्यत्वाभिनिवेशेन ये सर्वे आरम्भाः, तेषां फल-वैपरीत्यं पश्येत् । एवं फल-वैपरीत्याद् अकामः स्यात् ॥२॥
word_for_word: with the mind purified by one's own duties
through insistence that sense objects are real
entries.literal_english: How does desirelessness arise? After purifying the mind through one's own duties, one should observe that all undertakings of embodied beings, whose minds insist on the reality of sense objects, produce contrary results. Seeing this reversal of results, one becomes free from desire.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, काम्य-विषयाणां मिथ्यात्वाद् अपीत्य् आह---सुप्तस्येति । विफलोऽर्थ-शून्यः। अत्रैव प्रयोगः, इन्द्रियैर् या बहिर् नाना-बुद्धिः सा विफला, नानात्मकत्वात् ऐन्द्रियकत्वाच् च । मनो-जन्य-स्वप्न-मनोरथ-वद् इति ॥३॥
word_for_word: varied outward cognition through the senses
like a dream or mental fancy born from the mind
entries.literal_english: Desired objects are unreal, and therefore their pursuit is fruitless and without purpose. The same applies to the varied outward cognition produced by the senses: it is fruitless because it is manifold and sense-made, like a dream or a mental fancy arising from the mind.

entries.sanskrit:
मोक्षर्थी न प्रवर्तेत तत्र काम्य-निषिद्धयोः ।

नित्य-नैमित्तिके कुर्यात् प्रत्यवाय-जिहासया ॥ इति स्मृतिः ।

अतः प्रवृत्तं काम्यं कर्म त्यजेन् निवृत्तं नित्य-नैमित्तिकम् एव कुर्यात् । आत्म-विचारे तु सम्यक्-प्रवृत्तो निवृत्त-कर्म-चोदनाम् अपि नाद्रियेत ॥४॥
word_for_word: should perform obligatory and occasional duties
with the wish to avoid demerit
should perform only the obligatory and occasional action that remains
being properly engaged in inquiry into the Self
entries.literal_english: A seeker of liberation should not undertake desired or prohibited actions. He should perform obligatory and occasional duties to avoid demerit, abandoning desire-motivated action. But one who is properly engaged in inquiry into the Self need not even heed the injunctions governing the cessation of action.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, यमान् अहिंसादीन् अभीक्ष्णम् आदरेण सेवेत, शौचादींस् तु नियमान् क्वचित् यदा शक्तिस् तदा आत्म-ज्ञानाविरोधेन । यमान् द्वादशे, नियमांश् चैकोनविंशे ऽध्याये वक्ष्यति । किं च, यमेष्व् अप्य् आदरं परित्यज्य गुरुम् उपासीतेत्य् आह---मद्-अभिज्ञम् इति । मद्-आत्मकं मद्-रूपम् ॥५॥
word_for_word: the restraints in the twelfth and observances in the nineteenth
of My Self and of My form
entries.literal_english: One should constantly and respectfully practice the restraints beginning with nonviolence, and practice the observances beginning with purity when one has the ability and they do not obstruct Self-knowledge. Their fuller treatment will come later. Even more important is to serve a guru who knows Me and is of My very nature and form.

entries.sanskrit: गुरु-सेवकस्य धर्मान् आह---अमानीति । दक्षोऽनलसः । निर्ममो जायादिषु ममता-शून्यः । गुरौ तु दृढ-सौहृदः । असत्वरोऽव्यग्रः । अमोघ-वाक् व्यर्थालाप-रहितः । एतान्य् एव शिष्यस्य लक्षणानि ज्ञेयानि ॥६॥
word_for_word: the duties of one who serves the guru
without possessiveness toward wife and the rest
entries.literal_english: The duties and characteristics of a disciple are these: he does not seek honor, is capable and not lazy, has no possessiveness toward wife and others, is deeply affectionate toward the guru, is unhurried and unagitated, speaks effectively, and avoids useless talk.

entries.sanskrit: ननु स्व-जायादिषु कथं निर्ममः स्यात् तत्राह---जायेति । औदासीन्य-हेतुं विवेकं दर्शयति---आत्मनोऽर्थं प्रयोजनं सर्वत्र समम् इव पश्यन्न् इति । अयं भवः, सर्व-देहेष्व् आत्मन एकत्वाज् जायादि-देहेऽस्मिंश् च स्व-देहे आत्मनोऽर्थः सुखादिः सम एव केन विशेषेणैतेष्व् एव ममत्वाभिनिवेश इत्य् एवम् उदासीनः सन् गुरुं प्रपद्येतेति ॥७॥
word_for_word: toward one's own wife and the rest
how can one be without possessiveness
the purpose or interest of the Self
seeing as though it were equal everywhere
because the Self is one in all bodies
happiness and the rest are equal
entries.literal_english: How can one be without possessiveness toward one's wife and family? He should see the Self's purpose as equal everywhere. Since the Self is one in every body, the happiness and other interests found in the bodies of wife and family are not essentially different from those in one's own body. Seeing no valid distinction for possessiveness, he becomes detached and approaches the guru.

entries.sanskrit: अहो कोऽसौ देहादि-व्यतिरिक्त आत्मा यस्यैक्याद् अर्थः सर्वेषु समः स्यात् ? तम् आह---विलक्षण इति । स्थूल-सूक्ष्म-देह-द्वयाद् आत्मान्यो यतो विलक्षणः । द्वेधा वैलक्षण्यं दर्शयति---ईक्षिता स्व-दृग् इति । द्रष्टा हि दृश्याद् विलक्षणः । स्व-प्रकाशश् च जडाद् विलक्षणः । तयोर् अन्यत्वे दृष्टान्तः---यथाग्निर् दाहकः प्रकाशकश् च, दाह्यात् प्रकाश्यश् च दारुणः काष्ठात् । अन्यस् तद्वद् इति ॥८।
word_for_word: the Self distinct from the body and the rest
different from the two bodies, gross and subtle
the seer is distinct from the seen
the self-luminous is distinct from the inert
fire is the burner and illuminator
wood is what is burned and illuminated
the Self is other in the same way
entries.literal_english: The Self is distinct from the gross and subtle bodies. The seer is different from what is seen, and the self-luminous is different from what is inert. Fire both burns and illuminates, while wood is what is burned and illuminated; in the same way the Self is distinct from the body.

entries.sanskrit: अनेनैव दृष्टान्तेन नित्यत्वानादित्व-विभुत्वैकत्वादयोऽपि सिध्यन्तीत्य् आह---निरोधेति । यथा दारुष्व् अन्तः-प्रविष्टोऽग्निस् तत्-कृतान् नाशादीन् प्राप्नोति, न तु स्वतो नाशादिमान्। एवं देह-गुणान् अनित्यत्वादीन् देहात् परो नित्यादि-स्वरूपोऽप्य् आत्मानुभवति । ततश् च नित्यत्वादिभिर् अपि वैलक्षण्याद् अन्यत्वम् इति भावः ॥९॥
word_for_word: eternity, beginninglessness, all-pervasiveness, oneness and the rest
fire entered within pieces of wood
undergoes destruction and the other states caused by them
entries.literal_english: The same fire analogy proves the Self's eternity, beginninglessness, all-pervasiveness and oneness. Fire that has entered wood appears to undergo the destruction and other states of the wood, but it is not destroyed by itself. Similarly the Self, which is beyond the body and eternal by nature, appears to experience the body's impermanence and other qualities. Its difference from the body follows from that distinction.

entries.sanskrit: नन्व् अग्नेर् दारु-संयोगात् तद् धर्म-भाक्त्वं घटते, आत्मनस् त्वसङ्गत्वात् कथं देहेन तद् धर्मैर् वा संबन्धः, संबन्धे वा कुतस् तन् निवृत्तिस् तत्राह---योऽसाव् इति । पुरुषस्येश्वरस्याधीनैर् माया-गुणैर् योऽसौ सूक्ष्मोऽयं च स्थूलो देहो विरचितः पुंसो जीवस्यायं संसारस् तन् निबन्धनस् तद् अध्यास-कृतः । हि यस्माद् एवं तस्माद् आत्म-विद्या तन् निवर्तिकेत्य् आह---आत्मनो विद्य विज्ञानं तस्य छित् छेत्त्री । आच्छिद् इति वा पद-च्छेदः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: relation with the body and its properties
under the control of the Lord
the cutter; the feminine form is also read
entries.literal_english: One may ask how the unattached Self can be related to the body and share its properties, as fire shares those of wood. The subtle and gross bodies are made from the guṇas of Māyā under the Lord's control. The jīva's saṃsāra is bondage produced by superimposition. Knowledge of the Self cuts that superimposition; the final phrase may also be divided as a feminine form meaning “the cutter.”

entries.sanskrit: यस्माद् एवं तस्माज् जिज्ञासया विचारेण । आत्म-स्थम् आत्मनि कार्य-कारण-सङ्घात एव स्थितं सम्यग् ज्ञात्वा एतद् एतस्मिन् देहादौ वस्तु-बुद्धिं स्थूल-सूक्ष्म-क्रमेण निरसेत् त्यजेत् ॥११॥
word_for_word: situated in the aggregate of effects and causes
the notion of reality in this body and the rest
entries.literal_english: Since this is so, through inquiry one should correctly know the Self as present in the aggregate of effects and causes, and then remove the notion that this body and the rest are ultimate reality, proceeding through the gross and subtle levels.

entries.sanskrit: गुरोर् लब्धा विद्या अविद्या-तत्-कार्य-निरसन-क्षमेति स्फुटी-कर्तुं विद्योत्पत्तिम् अग्न्य्-उत्पत्ति-रूपकेण निरूपयति---आचार्य इति । आद्योऽधरः । तत्-सन्धानं तयोर् मध्यमं मन्थन-काष्ठम् । प्रवचनम् उपदेशः । विद्या तु सन्धिः, सन्धौ भवन्न् अग्निर् इव । तथा च श्रुतिः---आचार्यः पूर्व-रूपम् । अन्तेवास्य् उत्तर-रूपम् । विद्या सन्धिः । प्रवचनं सन्धानम् [तै।उ। १.३.३] इति ॥१२॥
word_for_word: capable of removing ignorance and its effects
through the metaphor of producing fire
the teacher is the first, lower piece
entries.literal_english: Knowledge received from the guru can remove ignorance and its effects. Its arising is explained through the metaphor of fire production: the teacher is the lower piece, the pupil the upper piece, their joining is the middle churning stick, instruction is the process of joining, and knowledge is the fire born at that junction. The cited Śruti assigns these same correspondences.

entries.sanskrit: अग्नि-सादृश्यम् एवाह---वैशारदीति । विशारदोऽति-निपुणस् तेन शिष्येण प्राप्ता तेन गुरुणोपदिष्टा वा अति-विशुद्धा बुद्धिर् गुण-कार्य-रूपां मायां निवर्तयति । यदात्मकम् एतद् विश्वं जीवस्य संसृति-निमित्तं तान् गुणंश् च दग्ध्वा असमिन् निरिन्धनः, तस्मात् कार्येण कारणेन विद्यय च व्यवधानाभावात् साक्षात् परमानन्द-रूपो भवतीति ॥१३॥
word_for_word: Māyā consisting of the effects of the guṇas
the cause of the jīva's transmigration
through effects such as body and senses
through knowledge of unity born from the sacred statement
directly of the nature of supreme bliss
entries.literal_english: The comparison is with fire. The highly purified intellect of a very capable disciple, attained through the guru's instruction, drives away Māyā made of the guṇa-effects and burns the guṇas that constitute the universe and cause the jīva's transmigration. It then disappears like fire without fuel. When the obstructions of the effects, such as body and senses, and the cause, ignorance, are absent through knowledge born from the unity of the sacred statement, the Self is directly realized as supreme bliss.

entries.sanskrit: एवं तावत् स्व-प्रकाश-ज्ञान-स्वरूपो नित्य एक एवात्मा, कर्तृत्वादयश् च धर्मास् तस्य देहोपाधिकास् तद्-व्यतिरिक्तं सर्वम् अनित्यं माया-मयं च । अतः सर्वतो विरक्तः सन्न् आत्म-ज्ञानेन मुच्यत इत्य् उक्तं, विलक्षणः स्थूल-सूक्ष्मात् [भा।पु। ११.१०.८] इत्य्-आदिना, तद् एव श्रुति-समन्वयेन निर्णीतेऽपि । अथ मतान्तर-विरोधेन सन्देहो मा भूद् इति तन्-मतं निराकर्तुम् उद्भावयति---अथेति ।
word_for_word: the Self is eternal and one
distinct from the gross and subtle
entries.literal_english: The Self alone is eternal, one, and of the nature of self-luminous knowledge. Doership and similar properties belong to it only through the body's limiting adjunct; everything apart from it is impermanent and Māyā-made. Thus one who is detached from all is liberated through Self-knowledge. The following discussion removes doubts by addressing rival doctrines, while the cited scriptural teaching confirms the Self's distinction from the gross and subtle bodies.

entries.sanskrit: न च सर्व-भोग्यानां विच्छेदान् मायामयत्वाद् वा वैराग्यं स्याद् इत्य् आह---सर्व-भावानां स्रक्-चन्दनादीनां संस्था स्थितिर् औत्पत्तिकी प्रवाह-रूपेण नित्या । तथा च वदन्ति---न कदाचिद् अनीदृशं जगत् इति । अतस् तत्-कर्ता कश्चिद् ईश्वरो नास्तीति भावः । किं च, यथा यथावत् । न तु मायामयीत्य् अर्थः । न चात्म-स्वरूप-भूतं नित्यम् एकं ज्ञानम् अस्तीत्य् आह---तत् तद् इति । घट-पटाद्याकार-भेदेन धीर् जायते, अतोऽनित्या भिद्यते च । अयं गूढोऽभिप्रायः । नहि नित्य-ज्ञान-रूप आत्मा, अपि तु ज्ञान-परिणामवान्, न च विकारित्वेनानित्यत्व-प्रसङ्गः । यथाहुः---विक्रिया-ज्ञान-रूपस्य न नित्यत्वे विरोत्स्यते इति । अतो मुक्ता-विनिद्र्यादि-रहितस्य परिणामासंभवाज् जडत्वेन तत्-प्राप्तेर् अपुरुषार्थत्वात् प्रवृत्तिर् एव श्रेयसी, न निवृत्तिर् इति ॥१५॥
word_for_word: because all objects of enjoyment perish
because they are made of Māyā
there is no creator of it, [the rival view says]
cognition arises through forms such as pot and cloth
activity alone is the higher good
entries.literal_english: The discussion answers the view that detachment could arise either because all enjoyables perish or because they are Māyā-made. It describes garlands, sandalwood and other entities as persisting in an originating stream, and cites the view that the world has never been otherwise and has no separate creator. It then argues that cognition varies with forms such as pot and cloth, while considering whether the Self is eternal knowledge or undergoes transformations of knowledge. Because a changeless, inert state would not be a meaningful human goal, the rival conclusion is that activity is superior, not cessation; this is the doctrinal position being presented for examination.

entries.sanskrit: तत्र तावद् उक्तम् अङ्गीकृत्य वैराग्योपपादनाय प्रवृत्ति-मार्गस्यानर्थ-हेतुत्वं प्रपञ्चयति---एवम् अपीत्य् आदिना लोकानां लोक-पालानाम् इत्य् अतः प्राक्तनेन ग्रन्थेन । अङ्ग हे उद्धव ! कालावयवतः संवत्सरादि-रूपात् ॥१६॥
word_for_word: the harmfulness of the path of activity
of the worlds and their guardians
in the form of a year and the rest
entries.literal_english: Accepting the preceding argument for the moment, he elaborates why the path of activity produces harm in order to establish detachment. The phrase beginning “even so” refers to the worlds and their guardians, whose existence depends on divisions of Time such as years. “O dear Uddhava” is the direct address.

entries.sanskrit: अत्रापीति । स्वातन्त्र्य-पक्षे दुष्कर्मणो दुःक-भोगस्य वासम्भवाद् इत्य् अर्थः॥१७॥
word_for_word: because the experience of suffering would otherwise be impossible
entries.literal_english: Here too the point concerns the position that the agent is independent: if the agent were truly independent, the painful result of an evil action could not be coherently accounted for. This is the intended meaning.

entries.sanskrit: ननु ये सम्यक् कर्म कर्तुं जानन्ति ते सुखिन एव । ये तु न जानन्ति त एव दुःखिन । इति चेत् तत्राह---नेति । विदुषाम् अपि क्वचित् सुखं न विद्यते, तथा मूढानाम् अपि दुःखं न विद्यते । अतो वयं कर्म-कुशलत्वात् सुखिन इति तेषां केवलं वृथैवाहङ्कार इत्य् अर्थः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: know how to perform action correctly
suffering is sometimes absent even for fools
happy because of skill in ritual action
entries.literal_english: Even the learned who know how to perform action correctly do not always have happiness, and even the foolish do not always have suffering. Therefore their pride that they are happy merely because they are skilled in action is useless.

entries.sanskrit: अङ्गीकृत्याप्य् आह---यदीति । तं योगम् उपायं न विदुर् यथा साक्षान् मृत्युर् न प्रभवेत् ॥१९॥
entries.literal_english: Even granting that people know the means of obtaining happiness and avoiding suffering, they do not know the method by which death itself would fail to overcome them.

entries.sanskrit: तथापि यावज् जीवं सुखं भविष्यतीति चेन् नेत्य् आह---को न्व् इति । यतोऽन्तिके वर्तमानो मृत्युः न तुष्टिदो न तुष्टिं ददाति । आघातं वध-स्थानं प्रति नीयमानस्य वध्यस्य स्रक्-चन्दनादि यथा न सुखयेत् ॥२०॥
word_for_word: “happiness will last as long as life”
the blow for one being led to the place of execution
entries.literal_english: If one says that happiness will continue for the duration of life, the answer is no: death is already near and gives no satisfaction. Just as garlands, sandalwood and similar comforts do not please a victim being led to the place of execution, no nearby object can provide lasting happiness.

entries.sanskrit: एवम् अस्मिल् लोके सुखं नास्तीत्य् उक्तं लोकान्तरेऽपि तथैवेत्य् आह---श्रुतम् इति । श्रुतं स्वर्गादि तद् अपि दुष्टम् । स्पर्धा पर-सुखासहनम् । असूया पर-गुणे दोषाविष्करणम् । अत्ययो नाशः । व्ययोऽपक्षयस् तैर् दुष्टम् । यद् वा, व्ययो नाशः, अत्ययोऽन्यस्यातिशयः, तं दृष्ट्वा तद्-अप्राप्त्या दुःखम् इत्य् अर्थः । किं च बहवोऽन्तराया वैगुण्यादि-रूपा विघ्ना यस्मिन् कामे सुखे तस्य भावस् तत्त्वं तस्मात् । कृषिर् यथा बहु-विघ्ना तद्वत् । बहु-सुखत्वेन श्रुतम् अपि निष्फलम् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: the promised heaven and the rest
envy or inability to tolerate another's happiness
having the form of defects and the rest
though heard to bring much pleasure, it is fruitless
entries.literal_english: The heaven promised in the scriptures is also defective. It contains envy, the inability to endure another's happiness, faultfinding, ending and decline. Desired pleasure has many obstacles and defects, just as agriculture has many hazards; therefore even what is heard to be greatly pleasurable can prove fruitless.

entries.sanskrit: विघ्न-वैगुण्याद्य्-अभावम् अङ्गीकृत्यापि नाश-दुःखं दुष्परिहरम् इत्य् आह---अन्तरायैर् इति पञ्चभिः । निर्जितं साधितम् ॥२२॥
word_for_word: even accepting the absence of obstacles and defects
entries.literal_english: Even if the absence of obstacles and defects in a religious act is granted, the pain of eventual loss is difficult to avoid. The attained celestial position is therefore now described.

entries.sanskrit: यज्ञैर् देवता इन्द्रादि-रूपा इष्ट्वा ॥२३॥
word_for_word: the deities in forms beginning with Indra
entries.literal_english: Having worshiped the deities, in forms beginning with Indra, through sacrifices, the sacrificer reaches the celestial destination described next.

entries.sanskrit: स्व-पुण्यैर् उपचिते सर्व-भोग-सम्पन्ने देवीनां मध्ये विहरन् गन्धर्वैर् उपगीयते ॥२४॥
word_for_word: is sung about by the Gandharvas
entries.literal_english: In the celestial region accumulated through his own merit and endowed with every enjoyment, he sports among the celestial women while the Gandharvas sing his praises.

entries.sanskrit: कामेनेच्छया गच्छता विमानेन । किङ्कणी-जाल-मालिना क्षुद्र-घण्टिका-समूह-शोभिना । सह स्त्रीभिः सुरा-क्रीडेषु नन्दनादिषु क्रीडन्न् आत्म-पातं न वेद ॥२५॥
word_for_word: by an aerial car moving according to desire
adorned with rows of small bells
beautified by groups of little bells
in divine pleasure gardens such as Nandana
does not know his own fall
entries.literal_english: Moving in an aerial car according to his desire, adorned with rows of small bells, he sports with women in divine pleasure gardens such as Nandana. So absorbed in this enjoyment, he does not know that his fall is approaching.

entries.sanskrit: कालेन चालितः पतितः ॥२६॥
entries.literal_english: When the accumulated merit is exhausted, he is moved by Time and falls.

entries.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिर् द्वि-विधा । विष्यनुसारेण काम्ये कर्मणि वा तल् लङ्घनेषु तल् लङ्घनेनाधर्मे वा । तत्र काम्य-प्रवृत्तेर् गतिर् उक्ता अधर्म-प्रवृत्तेर् गतिम् आह---यदीति । यदि वेत्य् अन्वयः । अजितेन्द्रियत्वात् कामात्मातः कृपणोऽतो लुब्धो भोग-तृष्णाकुलोऽतः स्त्रैणः स्त्री-लम्पटस् तद्-अर्थं भूत-विहिंसकः ॥ किं च, दुष्ट-जन-प्रलोभितो धनाद्य्-अर्थं पशून-विधिना हत्वा । तमः स्थावरतां याति ॥ एवं कर्मसु प्रवृत्तस्य न सुखं न च दुःख-निवृत्तिर् इत्य् उपसंहरति---कर्माणीति ॥२७-२९॥
word_for_word: in violation of that, in adharma
for one engaged in such actions
entries.literal_english: Activity is twofold: it follows sense objects through desire-motivated action, or it violates dharma and becomes adharma. The destination of desire-motivated activity has been stated; the destination of adharma is now given. Because his senses are uncontrolled, a person becomes desire-ridden, pitiable, greedy and tormented by thirst for enjoyment; he becomes addicted to women and harms living beings. Enticed by wicked people, he kills animals unlawfully for wealth and similar ends and enters darkness and immobile birth. Thus one engaged in these actions finds neither happiness nor release from suffering.

entries.sanskrit:
तथापि लोकानां नित्यत्वाद् अमर्त्य-धर्मत्वाच् च लोक-पालानां सुखम् अस्तीति चेत् तत्राह---लोकानाम् इति । द्वौ परार्धौ परमायुर् यस्य तस्य ब्रह्मणोऽपि । तथा च श्रुतिः---

> भीषाऽस्माद् वातः पवते, भीषोदेति सूर्यः । >
> भीषाऽस्माद् अग्निश् चेन्द्रश् च, मृत्युर् धावति पञ्चमः ॥ [तै।उ। > २.८.१] इति ।

अतः प्रवृत्ति-मार्गस्यैवम् अनर्थ-हेतुत्वाद् विरक्त्या ततो निवृत्तिर् एव युक्तेति तात्पर्यार्थः ॥३०॥
word_for_word: because the guardians have an immortal nature
the happiness of the guardians of the worlds
because the path of activity causes harm
entries.literal_english: Even if one argues that the worlds are eternal and their guardians have immortal natures, Brahmā himself has only two parārdhas as his maximum lifespan, and all cosmic powers act out of fear of the Supreme. Since the path of activity is therefore a cause of harm, withdrawal through detachment is the appropriate conclusion.

entries.sanskrit: एतेनैव स्वयम् ईश्वरत्वाविष्कारेण ईश्वराभवाङ्गीकारः परित्यक्तः । अन्यद् अपि प्रौढ्या पूर्वम् अङ्गी-कृतं निराकरोति चतुर्भिः । तत्र यद् उक्तं कर्तृ-भोक्तृ-रूप एवात्मेति तन् निराकरोति---गुणा इति । गुणा इन्द्रियाणि कर्माणि सृजन्ति, न त्व् आत्मा । आत्मैवेन्द्रियाणि प्रवर्तयन् कर्माणि करोतीति चेत्, नेत्य् आह---गुण इति । गुणः सत्त्वादिर् गुणान् इन्द्रियाण्य् अनुसृजते प्रवर्तयति, न त्व् आत्मा । अत आत्मनः कर्तृत्वं तावन् नास्ति । भोक्तृत्वम् अप्य् औपाधिकम् इत्य् आह---जीवस् त्व् इति । गुण-संयुक्त इन्द्रियादि-संयुक्तः । कुतः ? इत्य् अत आह---असौ तेष्व् अहङ्कारवान् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३१॥
word_for_word: the acceptance that God is absent
the Self as doer and enjoyer
the guṇas and senses produce actions
directs the senses according to the guṇas
enjoyership is due to an adjunct
entries.literal_english: The Lord's own manifestation of sovereignty has already rejected the view that there is no Lord. Four further verses refute the idea that the Self itself is the doer and enjoyer. The guṇas and the senses produce actions; the Self does not. A guṇa such as sattva directs the senses, so the Self has no independent agency. Its enjoyership is conditioned by an adjunct: the jīva is joined to the guṇas and becomes egoic in relation to them.

entries.sanskrit: यच् चोक्तम् आत्मनो नानात्वं तद् अप्य् औपाधिकम् इत्य् आह---यावत् स्याद् इति । गुणानां वैषम्यम् अहङ्कारादि-कार्य-रूपम् । नन्व् आत्मन एकत्वे कथं पारतन्त्र्यम् उक्तं ? कथं वा लोक-पालादीनाम् अपि मद्-भयम् इत्य् उक्तं ? तत्राह---नानात्वम् इति ॥३२॥
word_for_word: having the form of effects beginning with ego
fear of Me among the guardians of the worlds
entries.literal_english: The previously proposed multiplicity of the Self is only due to limiting adjuncts. The inequality of the guṇas appears as effects beginning with ego. Even though the Self is one, apparent multiplicity produces the jīva's dependence and explains why even the guardians of the worlds fear the Lord.

entries.sanskrit: यच् च गूढम् अभिप्रेतं प्रवृत्तिर् एव श्रेयसीति तत्राह---य एतद् इति । एतद् गुण-वैषम्यं तत् कृतं भोगं कर्म चेत्य् अर्थः । उपासीरन् सेवेरन् । ते लोकादीनाम् अनित्यत्वाच् छुचार्पिताः प्रोताः सन्तो मुह्यन्ति ॥३३॥
word_for_word: enjoyment and action produced by it
because the worlds and the rest are impermanent
entries.literal_english: The hidden claim that activity alone is beneficial is answered here. Those who serve the inequality of the guṇas, the enjoyment and karma produced by it, become bound and immersed in sorrow because the worlds and all such objects are impermanent; they therefore become deluded.

entries.sanskrit: न केवलम् अनित्यता-मात्रं किन्तु माया-मयत्वम् अपीत्य् आह---काल इति । स्वभावो देवत्वादि-परिणाम-हेतुः । धर्मस् तद् भोग-कारणम् । गुण-व्यतिकरे माया-क्षोभे सति माम् एव प्राहुर् न तु मद्-व्यतिरिक्ताः सन्ति ॥३४॥
word_for_word: the cause of transformation into godhood and the rest
in the disturbance of the guṇas
there are no things apart from Me
entries.literal_english: The objects are not only impermanent; they are Māyā-made. Time, nature and dharma are spoken of as causes of transformations such as godhood and as causes of the resulting enjoyment. When the guṇas are disturbed and Māyā is agitated, these names refer to the Lord alone; nothing exists apart from Him.

entries.sanskrit: ततो निवृत्तिर् एव मुक्ति-हेतुत्व-च्छ्रेयसीति सिद्धम् । एवं तावद् एक एवात्मा, तस्य च गुण-कार्य-देह-संबन्ध-कृतः संसारः, आत्म-ज्ञानाच् च मुक्तिर् इत्य् उक्तं, विलक्षणः स्थूल-सूक्ष्मात् [भा।पु। ११.१०.८] इत्य्-आदिना । तद् एव च मतान्तर-निरासेन दृढी-कृतम् अथैषां [भा।पु। ११.१०.१४] इत्य्-आदिना । तत्र पृच्छति---गुणेष्व् इति । अयम् अर्थः---गुणेष्व् असत्सु मुक्तिः सत्स्व् एव वा । आद्ये ज्ञान-साधनाभावान् न मुक्तिः । द्वितीये च गुणेषु वर्तमानोऽपि तत्-कार्य-देह-जेषु कर्मसु सुखादिषु च कथं न बध्येत । तथापि तैर् आकाश-वद् अनावृतत्वान् न बध्यत इति चेत् तर्हि बन्धो न संभवतीत्य् आह---अनपावृतः कथं बध्यत इति ॥३५॥
word_for_word: withdrawal is superior because it causes liberation
saṃsāra is produced by connection with a body made from the guṇas
made firm by refuting other doctrines
because the means of knowledge would be absent
only while the guṇas are present
because one is uncovered like space
entries.literal_english: Withdrawal is established as superior because it leads to liberation. There is one Self; saṃsāra is produced by its connection with a body made from the guṇas, and liberation comes through Self-knowledge. A question follows: if the guṇas are absent, there is no means for knowledge; but if they are present, how can one avoid bondage through the body's actions and pleasures? Saying that the Self is uncovered like space would make bondage impossible altogether, so the precise condition must be explained.

entries.sanskrit: यदि तु सत्स्व् एव तद्-अहङ्कारेण बध्यते, तन्-निवृत्त्या च मुच्यत इति मतं तर्हि तत् कथं ज्ञातव्यं ? इति पृच्छति । बद्धो मुक्ता वा कथं वर्तेत्य् आदि । किं भुञ्जीत कथं भुञ्जीत ? इत्य् अर्थः ॥३६॥
word_for_word: one is bound by identification with them
through removal of that one is liberated
entries.literal_english: If the guṇas are present, the person is bound through egoic identification with them and is liberated when that identification is removed. Uddhava therefore asks how a bound or liberated person behaves, what he enjoys, how he enjoys it, and how he moves through life.

entries.sanskrit: एतत् एतद् विषयं प्रश्नम् । किं च एक एवात्माऽनादि-गुण-संबन्धान् नित्य-बद्धः । मुक्ते जन्यत्वेऽनित्यत्व-प्रसङ्गान् नित्य-मुक्त इत्य् अप्य् अङ्गी-कार्यं स्यात् । तत्र मे भ्रमो भवतीत्य् आह---नित्य-बद्ध इति ॥३७॥
word_for_word: because of beginningless connection with the guṇas
entries.literal_english: The Self is one, yet because its connection with the guṇas is beginningless it is called eternally bound. But if liberation were something produced, it would be impermanent, so one would also have to accept that the Self is eternally free. Uddhava states that this apparent contradiction leaves him confused.
